title: Commerce issues frontier-model export-control framework by Q1 2027
body: The mid-June export-control freeze on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 -- imposed on a case-by-case directive that named no published rule, took both models offline for all foreign persons, and rested on what the company describes as verbal evidence of a narrow jailbreak -- exposes the absence of any codified standard for when a frontier model's capabilities trigger export controls. With a bipartisan House group now demanding Commerce Secretary Lutnick document the legal basis and national-security rationale, and security researchers publicly disputing that ordinary defensive code-analysis should be controllable, the pressure is toward a written, generally-applicable framework rather than ad-hoc per-model orders. The prediction is that by Q1 2027 the Commerce Department (BIS) publishes a formal capability-threshold framework -- a proposed rule, interim final rule, or detailed guidance -- defining which model capabilities and evaluation triggers bring a frontier model under export-control jurisdiction, the way the Export Administration Regulations already gate advanced AI chips. The competitive consequence is durable: a published threshold tells every US lab which capabilities carry deployment-blocking risk, shifting near-term foreign-market access toward whichever frontier systems sit below the line.

reasoning.because: Fable 5 / Mythos 5 were frozen by a case-by-case directive citing no published capability rule
reasoning.given: bipartisan House oversight plus researcher pushback pressures a codified standard over ad-hoc orders
reasoning.so_that: Commerce publishes a capability-threshold framework defining when a frontier model falls under export control
reasoning.landing: Commerce/BIS publishes the framework by Q1 2027 as a rule or formal guidance
reasoning.plain_language: After regulators pulled two Anthropic models with no clear rule, lawmakers are pushing the government to write down exactly when an AI model gets export-blocked.

summary: Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 were frozen with no published rule, prompting a bipartisan House demand that Commerce justify it. That pressure points toward Commerce publishing a framework by Q1 2027 defining when a frontier model's capabilities trigger export controls, like US chip rules.
